title: kv-cache-kernel-seqlen-debug-scratchpad-19
content:
Goal: track debugging for strange behavior when sequence length crosses ~3072 tokens. Intermittent failures and corrupted outputs observed in prod and locally when we hit certain seqlen patterns. Hypothesis: kv-cache indexing + kernel selection (fused/triton/flash) leads to an out-of-bounds or stale cache window for some attention kernel codepaths.

Repro summary:
- Model: redwood-7b-v2 (quantized int8 path)
- Hardware: A100-40GB; also repro on V100 in CI
- Workload: long prefix generation + streaming continuation; single-client, batch-size 1; prefix lengths vary (512, 2048, 3072, 4096)
- Failure point: beyond ~3072 tokens, sometimes output contains repeated garbage tokens, occasionally raises runtime error 'KV cache index out of range' or segmentation fault in attention kernel.

Commands / experiments tried (local and CI):
1) baseline: kernel auto-selection
python -m rwi.serving.run_inference \
  --model redwood-7b-v2 \
  --device cuda:0 \
  --batch-size 1 \
  --max-seq-len 4096 \
  --stream
(note: uses default kernel selection logic)

2) force different kernels via env / flag
RWI_ATTENTION_KERNEL=triton python -m rwi.serving.run_inference --model redwood-7b-v2 --max-seq-len 4096
RWI_ATTENTION_KERNEL=flash python -m rwi.serving.run_inference --model redwood-7b-v2 --max-seq-len 4096
RWI_ATTENTION_KERNEL=cutlass python -m rwi.serving.run_inference --model redwood-7b-v2 --max-seq-len 4096

Results: triton and flash show the issue consistently when prefix > 3072. cutlass seemed more stable in one run but later failed. Auto selection tends to pick triton for A100.

3) toggled kv-cache modes
RWI_KV_CACHE_MODE=prefix   (default)
RWI_KV_CACHE_MODE=window   (experimental rolling window)

Observation: window mode delays failure (appears around 3900) but still shows corruption. Prefix mode fails sooner.

4) smaller reproducer: script that writes deterministic tokens until failure
python tools/repro/kvcache_repro.py --model redwood-7b-v2 --seed 42 --target-len 4096
This prints token counts and when it detects non-monotonic kv index. Useful for stack traces.

Observed logs / error snippets:
- Runtime error
  RuntimeError: KV cache index out of range (idx=32769, capacity=32768)
  at rwi/serving/kv_cache.cpp:214
- CUDA assert seen in flash attention run
  CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at rwi/ops/flash_attention.cu:1034
- Repeated tokens sample:
  "... the the the the the \x00\x00\xFF ..."
- Trace shows attention kernel selected = triton, chunk_size=64, kv_offset=32768

Hypotheses (ordered):
1) Off-by-one in kv cache allocation with particular quantized model layout. When kernel path uses 32k boundary chunking (e.g., kv buffer grows in pages of 32768), an indexing + wrap bug triggers. Index 32769 > capacity 32768 suggests fencepost.
2) Kernel-specific optimization (triton/flash) uses different key/value packing order; mismatch between serving runtime's vmapped kv indexing and kernel's expected layout leads to stale reads once we cross a page boundary.
3) Streaming/continuous batching code calls into cache growth logic incorrectly when streaming token commits and eviction policies interact. Possible race in async GPU memcpy when acknowledging tokens back to user.
4) Quantization path (int8) uses smaller element size but still uses same capacity math; element_size vs stride mismatch causes wrong capacity computation.

Evidence for 1/2: stack traces consistently point at attention kernel entry, and when we force cutlass (simpler code path) the issue reduces. Also 'idx==capacity' errors aligned to 32768 boundary repeatedly.

Quick checks to run next (short tasks):
- Add asserts in kv_cache.cpp before growth: assert(idx < capacity) and log capacity/element_size/stride per allocation. Re-run repro to capture params.
- Dump kernel-config chosen by selector to logs (include chunk_size, dtype, packing, layout). Already partially logged but need full struct.
- Re-run with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to get precise stack traces for illegal address.
- Run the repro under ASAN (CPU-only) to verify indexing math on host before GPU path triggers.
- Validate calculation of capacity in quantized loader: element_size = get_element_size(dtype); capacity = allocated_bytes / element_size; confirm integer math doesn't floor incorrectly.
- Add unit test that simulates kv growth at exact 32768 boundary across kernels.

Longer investigations / TODOs:
- Compare the memory layout produced by the quantized model loader and the kernel's expected K,V shapes. Create a small translator to reserialize K/V buffer on CPU and verify per-index values.
- Audit kernel selection heuristics: if auto picks triton for sequence lengths near boundary, prefer cutlass for long-running streams until we fix packing.
- Consider moving growth/generation logic to preallocate headroom of +1 page to avoid idx==capacity on boundary.
- If root cause is element_size mismatch, fix in loader and add strict tests for all dtypes.

Notes from last debug session (2026-02-18):
- Alex reproduced on perf rig (A100) and attached gdb/cuda backtrace. He saw same idx==capacity at 32768.
- Ravi walked through kernel pack code and found a place where columns are padded to 64 but the runtime computed stride without padding for quantized layout; suspect mismatch there.
- I added logging in kernel_selector to dump reason for choosing kernel; output shows: reason=\"throughput_estimate:triton\" for long continuous streams. Need to include seqlen boundary heuristics.

Quick patch I tried (hotfix): when growing kv buffer, round up capacity to next page + 128 entries; this seems to hide the crash in several runs but doesn't actually fix packing mismatch. Not suitable for release without tests.

Files / PRs to reference:
- PR #1234 (attempt to add asserts/logging) - https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1234
- Repro script: tools/repro/kvcache_repro.py
- JIRA RWI-7890: \"KV cache OOB with long sequences\"

Next steps (priority):
1) Add detailed logging + assert (non-fatal) to capture capacity/idx/element_size/stride before kernel launch. Merge to canary.
2) Get deterministic CI run on V100 + A100 with forced triton/flash/cutlass.
3) If packing mismatch confirmed, align loader and kernel packers and add end-to-end memory comparison test.
4) Update kernel selector to avoid aggressive triton selection for streaming workloads until fixed.

Misc notes / brain dump:
- Might be related to chunk_size interplay: triton uses chunk_size 64 -> K/V per head per position becomes packed in contiguous windows; if growth occurs mid-chunk, kernel expects contiguous buffer and reads past valid region.
- Check K/V commit flow: commit to GPU happens in async cudaMemcpy2D. If we grow/resize on CPU then issue kernel before GPU copy completes, kernel might read stale/uninitialized pages. Use stream synchronization for a test.
- Also check for signed/unsigned mixing in index arithmetic (int vs size_t) in kv_cache.cpp.

If anyone picks this up: start with reproducer above, add assert logs, and run with RWI_ATTENTION_KERNEL=triton + CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1. I'm leaving the canary with additional logging on staging (tag: seqlen-kv-debug).
